key_insight: AdaPCLA improves longitudinal EHR generation for rare clinical events by adaptively calibrating priors and logits, helping autoregressive models better preserve tail co-occurrence patterns.
clinical_relevance: This could make synthetic EHR data more faithful for underrepresented patient subgroups, supporting privacy-preserving research and evaluation.
method: Uses adaptive prior-calibrated logit adjustment during training to better fit long-tailed EHR distributions.
Internalizes data knowledge through simulated annealing to retain useful prior signals.
Supports zero-shot distribution control for training-free adaptation across clinical populations.
evidence_signal: In real-world evaluations, AdaPCLA improved tail plausibility and downstream utility, including TailPairSeen gains over HALO of 114.2% on MIMIC-III and 65.1% on MIMIC-IV, plus a 3.5% F1 improvement for zero-shot cross-population adaptation.
watch_item: Performance depends on annealing speed and NTK conditioning, so careful tuning and validation are likely needed before deployment on new EHR datasets.
paper_title: AdaPCLA: Adaptive Prior-Calibrated Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Longitudinal EHR Generation
